title: Conjecture 1.2
context_text: A graph $G$ is $H$-Ramsey if every two-colouring of its edges contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and the $F$-Ramsey number $r_F(H)$ is the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $H$-Ramsey graph; $F$ a single vertex gives the Ramsey number and $F=K_2$ the size Ramsey number. $r(K_t)$ is the usual Ramsey number of $K_t$, so $K_{r(K_t)}$ is $K_t$-Ramsey and $r_{K_s}(K_t)\le\binom{r(K_t)}{s}$. Chvátal observed that $r_{K_2}(K_t)=\binom{r(K_t)}{2}$, i.e. the complete graph on $r(K_t)$ vertices minimises the number of edges among $K_t$-Ramsey graphs. Sam Spiro asked whether the analogue holds for $r_{K_s}(K_t)$, and the authors conjecture that it does, i.e. that $K_{r(K_t)}$ minimises the number of copies of $K_s$ among $K_t$-Ramsey graphs. The condition $s\le t$ is necessary, since there are $K_{t+1}$-free $K_t$-Ramsey graphs (Folkman), giving $r_{K_s}(K_t)=0$ for $s>t$. The authors prove the case $s=3$ for all sufficiently large $t$, via the result that for an absolute constant $K$ every graph of chromatic number at least $r$ in which every edge lies in at least $K$ triangles has at least $\binom r3$ triangles. For general $s\le t$ they prove $r_{K_s}(K_t)\ge2^{s(t-1)/2-1}$, and they do not believe their techniques extend to $s\ge4$.
paper_title: Triangle Ramsey numbers of complete graphs

title: q-color generalization of Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: The $q$-color generalization of the conjecture that $r_{K_s}(K_t)=\binom{r(K_t)}{s}$ for all $s\le t$ holds: for all $q\ge2$ and $s\le t$, the minimum number of copies of $K_s$ in a graph whose every $q$-colouring of the edges contains a monochromatic $K_t$ equals $\binom{r_q(K_t)}{s}$, where $r_q(K_t)$ is the $q$-color Ramsey number of $K_t$.
context_text: A graph $G$ is $H$-Ramsey if every two-colouring of its edges contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and the $F$-Ramsey number $r_F(H)$ is the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $H$-Ramsey graph; $F$ a single vertex gives the Ramsey number and $F=K_2$ the size Ramsey number. $r(K_t)$ is the usual Ramsey number of $K_t$, so $K_{r(K_t)}$ is $K_t$-Ramsey and $r_{K_s}(K_t)\le\binom{r(K_t)}{s}$. Chvátal observed that $r_{K_2}(K_t)=\binom{r(K_t)}{2}$, i.e. the complete graph on $r(K_t)$ vertices minimises the number of edges among $K_t$-Ramsey graphs. In the $q$-colour setting, $H$-Ramsey means that every $q$-colouring of the edges contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and $r_q(K_t)$ is the least $n$ such that every $q$-colouring of $E(K_n)$ contains a monochromatic $K_t$. The authors conjecture $r_{K_s}(K_t)=\binom{r(K_t)}{s}$ for all $s\le t$ (two colours) and prove it for $s=3$ and $t$ sufficiently large. They note that the $q$-colour generalizations of Chvátal's theorem, of their $s=3$ result and of their basic lemmas (a $K_t$-Ramsey graph has chromatic number at least $r(K_t)$, and in a minimal $K_t$-Ramsey graph every edge lies in a $K_t$) hold by the same proofs, and they also conjecture the $q$-colour generalization of the main conjecture. The paper does not write the $q$-colour statement explicitly; the formulation above is the natural one.
notes: Stated in prose without a formal label. The paper text reads 'the q-color generalization of Theorem 1.2', which is almost certainly a typo for 'Conjecture 1.2', since no Theorem 1.2 exists in this paper. No explicit formula for the q-color version is given in the extracted text.
